name: Migraine Episode

demographic_risk.risk_explanation: Migraines occur up to 3 times more frequently in females, particularly during reproductive and young adult years.

description: A neurological condition marked by severe, pulsating unilateral or bilateral head pain, visual auras, and intense sensory hypersensitivity.

measurements_and_cures.overview: Sensory resting, cold compress therapy, hydration, and trigger elimination.
immediate_home_measures: Rest in a completely dark, quiet room.
Apply a cold ice pack to forehead and temples for 15-20 minutes.
Sip cold electrolyte water or ginger tea for nausea.
Practice slow rhythmic diaphragmatic breathing.
dietary_lifestyle_adjustments: Avoid aged cheeses, artificial sweeteners, nitrates, and alcohol.
Maintain strict regular sleep and eating schedules.
Reduce screen brightness and use blue-light filtering.
when_to_see_doctor: Sudden explosive thunderclap headache reaching maximum severity in seconds.
Headache accompanied by high fever, confusion, or weakness.
Attacks occurring more than 3 times per week.
typical_medical_treatments: Triptans or CGRP antagonists prescribed for acute abortive therapy.
Preventative beta-blockers or neuromodulators for recurrent attacks.
prevention_tips: Keep a daily migraine trigger diary.
Stay consistently hydrated with 2.5 liters of water daily.

name: Seasonal Influenza (Flu)

demographic_risk.risk_explanation: Affects both genders; highest severity in young children and adults over 65.

description: A contagious viral respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses infecting the throat, nose, and lungs with sudden high fever, chills, and severe aches.

measurements_and_cures.overview: Strict bed rest, oral rehydration, antipyretics, and early antiviral assessment within 48 hours.
immediate_home_measures: Stay strictly in bed; physical rest speeds immune recovery.
Drink warm broths, electrolyte water, and herbal teas.
Use lukewarm sponge baths to manage fever comfortably.
Use a cool-mist room humidifier to ease throat dryness.
dietary_lifestyle_adjustments: Eat light, easily digestible meals: bananas, rice, toast, and soups.
Isolate at home until fever-free for 24 hours without medication.
when_to_see_doctor: Shortness of breath, blue lips/face, or persistent chest pressure.
Confusion or inability to wake up.
Symptoms initially improve but return worse with deep chest coughing.
prevention_tips: Receive the annual seasonal influenza vaccine.
Wash hands frequently with soap for at least 20 seconds.

name: Acute Upper Respiratory Infection (Common Cold)

demographic_risk.risk_explanation: Very common worldwide across all ages and genders.

description: A benign, self-limiting viral infection of the nose and throat causing nasal congestion, sneezing, tickly cough, and mild malaise.

measurements_and_cures.overview: Warm saline gargles, nasal irrigation, rest, and abundant fluids.
immediate_home_measures: Gargle with warm salt water 3-4 times a day.
Inhale steam from a hot shower or facial steamer.
Use sterile saline nasal spray to clear congestion.
Drink warm water with raw honey and lemon.
dietary_lifestyle_adjustments: Eat vitamin C-rich fruits and warm soups.
Get 8-9 hours of restful sleep.
when_to_see_doctor: Fever lasting longer than 4 days or exceeding 102°F.
Severe earache or cheekbone sinus pain.
Difficulty swallowing or breathing.
typical_medical_treatments: OTC decongestants, saline rinses, and throat lozenges.

name: Acute Gastroenteritis (Stomach Bug)

demographic_risk.risk_explanation: Highly contagious viral or bacterial illness affecting all age groups.

description: Inflammation of the stomach and intestines causing acute diarrhea, cramping, and vomiting.

measurements_and_cures.overview: Oral rehydration solution (ORS) to prevent electrolyte depletion.
immediate_home_measures: Withhold solid food for the first 3 hours after vomiting.
Take small, frequent sips of ORS electrolyte solution.
Place a warm compress on the abdomen to soothe cramps.
dietary_lifestyle_adjustments: Follow the BRAT diet (Bananas, Rice, Applesauce, Toast).
Avoid dairy, greasy foods, caffeine, and spices for 72 hours.
when_to_see_doctor: Inability to keep liquids down for >12 hours.
Signs of severe dehydration: dry mouth, sunken eyes, no urination.
Visible blood in stool or high fever.
typical_medical_treatments: IV fluids if oral intake fails.
prevention_tips: Thorough hand hygiene before meals and after restroom use.

name: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD / Acid Reflux)

demographic_risk.risk_explanation: More common in adults, people with elevated BMI, or late-night eaters.

description: Chronic digestive disease where stomach acid flows back into the food pipe, irritating the lining and causing painful heartburn.

measurements_and_cures.overview: Meal timing, elevating head of bed, and antacid management.
immediate_home_measures: Do not lie down for 3 hours after eating.
Elevate head of bed by 6 inches.
Loosen tight clothing around waist.
dietary_lifestyle_adjustments: Eat smaller, frequent meals.
Avoid chocolate, mint, citrus, tomatoes, caffeine, and fried foods.
when_to_see_doctor: Difficulty or pain swallowing.
Unexplained weight loss or vomiting blood.
Chest pain radiating to the jaw or arm.
typical_medical_treatments: Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs) or H2 blockers.
prevention_tips: Avoid late dinners and maintain healthy weight.

name: Urinary Tract Infection (Cystitis / UTI)

demographic_risk.risk_explanation: Significantly more common in females due to shorter urethral anatomy.

description: A bacterial infection of the urinary bladder and urethra causing painful, burning sensations and frequent urgent needs to urinate.

measurements_and_cures.overview: Hydration, flushing bacteria, and targeted antibiotic therapy.
immediate_home_measures: Drink 2-3 large glasses of water immediately to flush bacteria.
Do not hold urine; empty bladder frequently.
Apply warm heating pad over pelvis.
dietary_lifestyle_adjustments: Avoid coffee, alcohol, and spicy foods.
Wipe from front to back.
when_to_see_doctor: High fever, shaking chills, or nausea.
Upper back/flank pain (kidney infection warning).
Visible pink or red blood in urine.

name: Kidney Stones (Renal Calculi)

demographic_risk.risk_explanation: More prevalent in men and individuals with low water intake or high sodium diets.

description: Hard mineral deposits formed inside kidneys that cause excruciating flank and back pain when moving through the ureter.

measurements_and_cures.overview: Copious fluid intake, medical expulsive therapy, and pain relief.
immediate_home_measures: Drink 2-3 liters of water per day.
Apply heat to affected flank to ease smooth muscle spasms.
Strain urine to catch passed stones for lab analysis.
dietary_lifestyle_adjustments: Reduce dietary sodium and animal protein.
Add fresh lemon juice to water (citrate inhibits stone crystals).
when_to_see_doctor: Excruciating pain making it impossible to sit still.
Complete inability to urinate.
Fever with flank pain.
prevention_tips: Keep daily urine clear and pale with consistent water intake.

name: Iron-Deficiency Anemia

demographic_risk.risk_explanation: Disproportionately affects females of childbearing age due to menstrual blood loss.

description: Inadequate healthy red blood cells caused by lack of iron, preventing efficient oxygen delivery to muscles and brain.

measurements_and_cures.overview: Iron repletion, vitamin C pairing, and CBC/Ferritin monitoring.
immediate_home_measures: Pace daily activities and take scheduled rest breaks.
Stand up slowly to avoid orthostatic dizziness.
Wear warm socks and gloves.
dietary_lifestyle_adjustments: Eat iron-rich foods: lentils, spinach, beans, tofu, lean meats.
Pair with Vitamin C (citrus, peppers) to multiply absorption.
Do not drink tea/coffee with meals.
when_to_see_doctor: Chest pain or rapid heartbeat during mild exertion.
Fainting spells or black tarry stools.
typical_medical_treatments: Prescription oral or IV iron supplements.
prevention_tips: Eat a well-rounded diet with diverse iron sources.

name: Atopic Dermatitis & Eczema

demographic_risk.risk_explanation: Affects children, teens, and adults, often linked with allergies.

description: A chronic inflammatory skin condition causing red, intensely itchy, dry, and scaly epidermal patches.

measurements_and_cures.overview: Ceramide barrier moisturizers, gentle skin cleansing, and trigger avoidance.
immediate_home_measures: Take short lukewarm showers (never hot water).
Apply thick ceramide cream within 3 minutes of showering.
Use cold damp compresses to soothe itchiness.
dietary_lifestyle_adjustments: Wear 100% breathable cotton clothing.
Use fragrance-free hypoallergenic detergents.
when_to_see_doctor: Yellow crusting or oozing on rash (bacterial infection).
Severe itching disrupting sleep.
typical_medical_treatments: Mild topical corticosteroids or calcineurin inhibitors.

name: Hypothyroidism (Underactive Thyroid)

demographic_risk.risk_explanation: Women are 5-8 times more likely to develop thyroid disorders.

description: Underactive thyroid gland failing to produce adequate thyroid hormone, slowing down metabolism, body heat, and energy.

measurements_and_cures.overview: TSH & Free T4 blood evaluation and daily synthetic thyroid hormone repletion.
immediate_home_measures: Dress in warm layers.
Keep a daily energy and symptom log.
dietary_lifestyle_adjustments: Ensure adequate dietary iodine and selenium.
High-fiber diet and regular gentle walking.
when_to_see_doctor: Enlarging visible neck swelling (goiter).
Extreme fatigue or slow heart rate.
typical_medical_treatments: Daily Levothyroxine tablet on an empty stomach.
prevention_tips: Periodic thyroid screening during wellness checks.

name: Essential Hypertension (High Blood Pressure Warning)

demographic_risk.risk_explanation: More common in adults over 40 due to arterial stiffening and lifestyle factors.

description: Persistently high arterial blood pressure straining blood vessels and vital organs.

measurements_and_cures.overview: DASH low-sodium diet, home blood pressure monitoring, and medical care.
immediate_home_measures: Sit quietly with feet flat for 5 minutes.
Take deep 4-second inhales and 6-second exhales.
Measure and log blood pressure.
dietary_lifestyle_adjustments: Follow DASH diet rich in potassium.
Strictly limit sodium under 1,500mg daily.
30 minutes of daily brisk walking.
when_to_see_doctor: Blood pressure reading over 180/120 mm Hg (Emergency).
Chest pain or visual disturbances.
typical_medical_treatments: Prescription antihypertensives (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, Calcium Channel Blockers).

name: Gout (Acute Uric Acid Arthritis)

demographic_risk.risk_explanation: Occurs 4-5 times more often in adult men, triggered by uric acid crystallization.

description: Painful inflammatory arthritis caused by uric acid crystals depositing in joints, most often the big toe.

measurements_and_cures.overview: Anti-inflammatory relief during acute flares, followed by long-term uric acid reduction.
immediate_home_measures: Elevate foot and remove all pressure from the toe.
Apply ice pack wrapped in towel for 20 minutes.
Drink 3 liters of water to help kidneys excrete uric acid.
dietary_lifestyle_adjustments: Avoid shellfish, red meat, beer, and high-fructose corn syrup.
Drink tart cherry juice and low-fat milk.
when_to_see_doctor: First sudden attack of excruciating joint pain.
High fever with joint swelling.
typical_medical_treatments: Colchicine or NSAIDs for acute attacks; Allopurinol for prevention.
